- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reverting trends; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 5-day avg is > 10% above 30-day moving avg.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment is mixed or trending sideways.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
